takeaways: Record second quarter: revenue of $1.44 billion was up 27%, Arm's fifth straight quarter of 20%+ growth, and adjusted EPS of $0.52 beat the $0.47 estimate (Investing.com).
Licensing did the heavy lifting, up 50% to $773 million. Royalties grew a slower 8% to $670 million, though data center royalties doubled year over year.
Guidance of $0.56 EPS and $1.54 billion revenue (at the midpoints) sits right on the $0.55 and $1.53 billion consensus, which Investing.com said is why the stock slipped after hours: no blowout.

GAAP EPS was only $0.12, weighed down by $46.6 million in losses on listed equity investments and Arm China credit charges, against a year-ago quarter that had a $131 million one-time gain (24/7 Wall St.).
Arm is moving into making its own chips: its AGI CPU has purchase orders running through calendar 2027 and first commercial deliveries on track for fiscal Q4 2027, per the shareholder letter.
verdict: Arm posted a record quarter and guided right where Wall Street was already standing, which for a stock priced like a moonshot counts as a mild disappointment. Licensing up 50% is great; royalties up 8% is the part that pays rent. Now it wants to build its own chips, which is a bit like a landlord deciding to also run the restaurant.

sources.title: Investing.com: Arm stock slips after hours as lack of blowout guidance offsets quarterly results
